regular plural inflection and spelling allomorphy (-s, -es, consonant-y to -ies)

grammatical-number and inflectional features, probes, and steering directions
regular-plural.explicit_gap: Close work maps grammatical number either as a representation (linearly decodable, steerable inflection subspaces across models including Pythia) or as agreement circuits that read a subject's number to choose a verb or reflexive form (SAE feature circuits in Pythia-70M, causal mediation and circuit probing in GPT-2, head/neuron accounts in Gemma-2B, DAS causal variables across Pythia scales). None locates the head/MLP-level mechanism by which an unmodified Pythia-70M reads a numeral or quantifier cue and selects the inflected noun form itself, none predicts held-out multi-component interventions for that behavior prospectively, none reconstructs the behavior from the proposed components, none tests self-repair or backup paths for it, and none quantifies the unexplained residual. The proposed Experiment 005 contribution is therefore a component-level, repair-aware, reconstruction-tested causal account of count-cued noun number selection with prospectively predicted held-out interventions and explicit residual accounting; it is not a novelty claim about grammatical number representations, which are already mapped.

close_work.absent_contribution: Li and Subramani (ACL 2026) probe and steer inflectional features including Plural across 25 models including Pythia; they establish a compact linear inflection subspace but give no head/MLP-level circuit for count-cued noun inflection, no held-out intervention predictions, no reconstruction, and no self-repair analysis.

Marks et al. (ICLR 2025) discover sparse feature circuits for subject-verb number agreement in Pythia-70M with ablation-based faithfulness and completeness; the behavior is verb selection from a subject's number in an SAE feature basis, not numeral/quantifier-cued noun inflection, and the circuits are not tested for held-out intervention prediction, reconstruction, or self-repair.

Arora, Jurafsky, and Potts (ACL 2024) benchmark causal methods on agreement and other SyntaxGym tasks across Pythia scales using DAS-found subspaces; they localize causal variables for agreement, not a component-level generation mechanism for noun number, and report no reconstruction or self-repair analysis.

Lepori et al. (circuit probing) identify and ablate subject-verb and reflexive number circuits in GPT-2 Small/Medium; different model family and agreement direction, no numeral-cued noun inflection, no held-out intervention prediction.
Finlayson et al. (ACL 2021) use causal mediation on GPT-2 and XLNet neurons for subject-verb agreement; neuron-level mediation for verb agreement only, no noun inflection, no circuit reconstruction.

Ferrando and Costa-jussa (EMNLP Findings 2024) find an attention head writing a subject-number direction read by final MLP neurons in Gemma-2B for subject-verb agreement; different model, verb agreement rather than noun inflection, no repair-aware or reconstruction test.
Mueller et al. (2022) analyze syntactic agreement neurons causally in multilingual models; verb agreement neurons, not count-cued noun inflection in Pythia.
